# Scientific review

**Correctness — PASS.** Geometric smoothness of a ternary quartic is equivalent to surjectivity in degree ten of the ideal generated by the equation and its partial derivatives, by the regular-sequence socle-degree bound. The C++ program enumerates all \(32{,}767\) nonzero equations, identifies \(10{,}920\) smooth members, and exhaustively counts triples closed under addition. Independent Walsh-convolution counting reproduces both the total \(5{,}796{,}728\) and the eight rational-base counts. Exact projective substitutions give the fixed-pencil counts; Burnside and subgroup-normalizer counting prove the four stabilizer strata. Gröbner tests independently verify the \(78\) projective orbits classified as smooth, on three charts each. The Fourier and Gröbner checks have the dependency and scope limitations stated in the verification notes.

**Originality — PASS, with priority risk.** The closest primary papers are Asgarli–Ghioca (arXiv:2203.07169), which proves smooth-pencil existence, and Nart–Ritzenthaler (arXiv:math/0312366), which classifies individual genus-three quartics. Neither inspected result states this finite-field census of pencil subspaces, its \(34{,}539\) projective orbits, stabilizer spectrum, or rational-base distribution. The general existence/dimension result (arXiv:2207.00918) and the nonblocking pencil result (arXiv:2301.09215) do not imply exact counts. The prior eight plane-filling pencils comprise one contained orbit, not the full population. Unindexed equivalent enumeration and uninspected older computational tables remain risks; no database partition establishes novelty.

**Value — PASS.** The result answers a natural finite-field refinement of the published smooth-linear-system problem: it measures the complete population of genus-three smooth pencils over the smallest field, distinguishes all rational-base point counts and determines the full orbit-size distribution rather than only examples or the number of individually smooth curves. In particular the absence of even-order stabilizers and the unique order-\(21\) orbit describe rigid geometric structure not contained in existing existence theorems.

**Scope and reproducibility.** This is an equation-level fixed-coordinate classification of projective pencils. It does not classify abstract curve triples, geometric base-scheme multiplicities or other fields. Independent audit and historical-priority certification are not claimed.

Self-review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.
